evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never frames the 10-15 minute timeframe, promise of dependable quote, or asks for confirmation before diving into details. Moves straight into 'So first is your requested date. It's Saturday October 7th, is that correct?'
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Maria), moving day (October 17th), city-to-city (2929 West Lane to 1616 Post Oak Boulevard), size (800 sq ft) — all four confirmed.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep goes directly into 'So first is your requested date' with no open-ended concern discovery before probing logistics.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (one-bedroom apartment), floor/stories (24th floor source, 14th floor destination), number of rooms (one bedroom + study), walking distance ('few steps'), additional rooms (study covered), special considerations (elevator reserved, loading dock, freight elevator), box count (25-35 range appropriate).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Asked: 'would you also need help packing up those boxes or all the boxes going to be ready to go?' Customer answered boxes ready to go.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Asked: 'typically for a one bedroom in a study there's about 25 to 35 pre pack boxes do you think you're gonna forward within the range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides both anchor and personalization: 'typically moving a one bedroom apartment takes two and a half to three and a half hours with two movers in your case, since you're moving from May 24th floor to a working floor unit, the elevators are reserve but I would want to estimate to move to take about three to five hours with you guys to be on the safer side. So you're going to be looking at around $612 to $1,020'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rate disclosed ($204/hour for two movers), all inclusions listed (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrapping, padding, floor runners, disassembly/reassembly, tools, no credit card/transportation/stair/elevator/disassembly fees), 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increment prorating explained.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Asked: 'Does that feel fair?' Customer responds 'Yes ma'am' — silence held.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No version of 'Does that put those to rest?' asked. Section 5 is skipped entirely.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Never asked. Rep moves directly from the estimate into the ask.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Never asked. No 'anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Asked plainly without an out: 'would you like our help with your move?' Customer confirms 'Yes.'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Mentioned: 'no need for deposit as well' — rate is locked by the booking confirmation.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Date (October 17th Saturday), time window (8:30-9am start), confirmation email promised, no addresses re-confirmed in the booking close itself. Missing explicit phone number confirmation, crew size confirmation (implied as 2 movers but not re-stated), and notes about customer concerns left for crew. Rep says 'I'll send the confirmation email with all the details and just double-check on your end' but the conversation itself does not explicitly re-confirm all details.

top_strength: Danah executed a complete, well-anchored logistics discovery and delivered a personalized, transparent estimate with all pricing framing intact, landing the close cleanly on the first ask.
coaching_note: Section 2 (Their Agenda and active listening reflection) was entirely skipped — rep must open with 'What are your biggest concerns about this move?' before probing, and Section 5 (Two Promises) was completely omitted, leaving the On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage undelivered; add these as non-negotiable stops on every call.
